_comment: T.A.R. capability/engine registry. Every capability that needs software T.A.R. does NOT ship is declared here. The UI reads `tar_caps.py caps` and locks anything with no installed engine behind a wall; the two wall buttons map to `engines <cap>` (ask the LLM to pick one) and `connect <cap>` (LLM searches + wires whatever is present). Package names verified against CachyOS/Arch repos + AUR on 2026-09-26. size_mb is download+install footprint, approximate.

tts.label: Speech out
tts.blurb: Lets T.A.R. talk back out loud.

piper.desc: Neural TTS. Sounds like a real voice, not a robot. Needs a voice file (auto-fetched).

espeak-ng.desc: Tiny and instant. Unmistakably a 1980s robot. Good fallback / good for a JARVIS-ish bite.

flite.desc: Festival-lite. Small, slightly warmer than espeak.

festival.desc: Older full TTS stack. Heavier than flite for little gain.

stt.label: Microphone / speech in
stt.blurb: Lets you talk to T.A.R. instead of typing.

whisper-cpp.desc: Whisper in C++. Accurate, offline, runs fine on CPU. Needs a model file (base.en ~78MB, auto-fetched).

vosk.desc: Lighter than Whisper and truly streaming, but less accurate. Good on a potato.

camera.label: Camera
camera.blurb: Lets T.A.R. open a live view or grab a still.

ffmpeg.desc: Grabs stills and clips off /dev/video*. Already on this box.

mpv.desc: Live camera window. Already on this box.

vision.label: Eyes (image understanding)
vision.blurb: Lets T.A.R. actually describe what the camera or a screenshot shows.

gemini.desc: Gemini sees your screen and camera (cloud mode, uses your free Gemini key).

moondream.desc: Tiny vision model. Fits this 7GB box alongside the rice. Describes scenes and reads big text.

llava-7b.desc: Much sharper, but 4.7GB will fight the rice for RAM on this machine.

qwen2vl-2b.desc: Better OCR than moondream, a bit heavier.

wakeword.label: Wake word
wakeword.blurb: Always-listening "hey tar" trigger. Needs the mic working first.

openwakeword.desc: Local 'hey jarvis' detector (openWakeWord). Runs offline, ~1-2% CPU.

cloud.label: Cloud brain
cloud.blurb: Swap the local model for Claude over the API. Far smarter and far faster than anything this machine can run locally — needs an API key and costs money per use.

anthropic.desc: Official Anthropic SDK. Installed into T.A.R.'s own venv, never the system python.

mouse.label: Mouse
mouse.blurb: Lets T.A.R. click, scroll and press buttons on screen for you.

wlrctl.desc: Tiny Wayland tool for a virtual mouse. Built for your user only -- no password needed.

voices._comment: Piper voice files, fetched on demand into ~/.local/share/bite-os/tar/voices/.

en_US-lessac-medium.desc: Neutral US male. Calm, butler-ish. Good default for T.A.R.

en_GB-alan-medium.desc: British male. The closest thing to actual JARVIS.

base.en.desc: English-only base. Best accuracy-per-MB for dictation on CPU.

tiny.en.desc: Half the size, noticeably worse on names and jargon.

small.en.desc: Clearly better, but slow on a CPU-only 7GB box.
